summary: Morning in the Safe Cave: Bjorn wakes after Gunnar and the two male Kin have already taken care of breakfast and laundry, leaving him coffee but no obvious job.
settingText: Bushwick studio apartment, early morning: sleeping area, tiny kitchenette/table, brass key by the door, books, laundry and groceries accumulated from Issue 5.

panelPlan.location: Safe Cave sleeping area opening onto kitchenette
panelPlan.action: Early morning across the whole studio. Gunnar pours coffee. First Male Kin finishes slicing bread at the tiny table. Second Male Kin ties a laundry bag and checks the brass key near the door. Bjorn sits up from bedding at frame edge; Astrid is not present.
Bjorn crosses to the table and reaches for the bread knife just as First Male Kin finishes cutting and slides the bread into a bowl.

panelPlan.location: Safe Cave doorway side of kitchenette
panelPlan.action: Bjorn turns toward the laundry bag; Second Male Kin shoulders it before Bjorn can take it.
Gunnar hands Bjorn a paper coffee cup. Bjorn accepts it; behind them First Male Kin clears the breakfast area and Second Male Kin settles the laundry bag on his shoulder.
Bjorn stands motionless with the coffee held at chest height. Behind him Gunnar turns back to the table while the two male Kin continue their tasks without looking toward Bjorn.

dialogueInline.text: I will do that.
It is done.
Then I will carry that.
I am carrying it.
Coffee remains.
Coffee is not work.

directionInline: Only Gunnar, Bjorn and the two established male Kin are visible. Astrid is off-page; do not add another Kin.

summary: At the neighborhood bodega, Bjorn tries to repay old kindness with labor and is stopped because the delivery already belongs to someone else's job.
settingText: Recurring Bushwick bodega: front counter, narrow delivery aisle and sidewalk delivery area in ordinary morning light.

panelPlan.action: A delivery worker wheels beverage crates toward the back through the narrow aisle. Bjorn enters with his familiar coffee cup; the Bodega Owner nods from the counter.
The delivery worker works a loaded hand truck around a tight turn. Bjorn immediately steps toward the cart.
Before Bjorn can take the hand truck, the Bodega Owner plants one hand on it and stops him. The worker still has control of the load.
The delivery worker keeps one hand tight on the hand-truck grip, jaw set. The owner holds one forearm across Bjorn's path, leaving the worker a clear lane.
The owner scans Bjorn's usual items. Bjorn stands square to the counter with direct eye contact, hands still at his sides as he answers.

dialogueInline.text: Morning.
No.
He is overmatched.
He is working. You are shopping.
You fed us before our money had meaning.
And you came back every morning and paid me. That's called being a customer. Stop trying to turn everything into a blood debt.
I said nothing of blood.
You had the face.

directionInline: The delivery worker is an ordinary working adult, not comic relief and not physically helpless.

summary: Back at the apartment, Carrie hears Bjorn say plainly that everyone else now provides the things he once understood as his responsibility.
settingText: Safe Cave, late morning: table, window and ordinary household clutter from the established apartment.

panelPlan.action: Carrie enters with a thin folder and grocery receipt. Gunnar reads at the table. First Male Kin repairs a loose bag strap. Bjorn stands at the window with empty hands; Second Male Kin and Astrid are out.
Carrie puts the folder down and looks toward Bjorn when he does not react.
Bjorn turns from the window and gives one restrained sweep of his hand toward the apartment, his face serious and still.
Carrie listens without correcting him. Bjorn indicates Gunnar and the working Kin with a small sweep of his hand.
Carrie watches Bjorn as she says the word “ornamental.” His brow tightens at the unfamiliar word; after his reply, she supplies the simpler word “decorative.”

dialogueInline.text: I brought the deeply glamorous renewal notice for the smoke detector inspection.
Okay. This is usually where you object to being inspected by a man with a clipboard.
Water comes through walls. Heat comes from iron. Food comes from the shop downstairs. Roads carry us. Paper grants the room.
Gunnar knows the city. They know the shops. You know the law. What remains for me?
You think if you're not necessary, you're ornamental.
I do not know that word.
Decorative.
Then no.

directionInline: Only First Male Kin is visible among the Kin on this page. Second Male Kin and Astrid are off-page.

summary: A cheap power strip sparks and is already made safe before Bjorn can act; after the danger is over, he smashes it and frightens the household.
settingText: Safe Cave kitchenette and sleeping edge, daytime. Ordinary apartment scale; the electrical fault is minor and contained.

panelPlan.location: Safe Cave kitchenette floor beside table
panelPlan.action: A cheap overloaded power strip gives one sharp spark and a small puff of gray smoke beside the table. No flame develops.
Gunnar immediately pulls the wall plug while First Male Kin lifts nearby bedding away in one motion.
The smoke is gone. The unplugged, inert power strip lies on the floor while Carrie, Bjorn, Gunnar and both male Kin look down at it.
Bjorn bends, picks up the dead strip and stares at it. His jaw tightens; nobody is asking him to do anything.

panelPlan.location: Safe Cave bare wall beside kitchenette
panelPlan.action: Bjorn slams the plastic strip once into the bare wall. The casing cracks. First Male Kin jerks backward; Second Male Kin freezes with hands half-raised; Carrie flinches; Gunnar remains still with the unplugged cord.

Carrie steps within arm’s length of Bjorn. Behind her, First Male Kin shifts behind the table edge, Second Male Kin keeps several feet of distance, and Gunnar stays still with the unplugged cord in hand.

dialogueInline.text: Dead.
That was not protection.
It failed this house.
Gunnar already protected the house.
You scared everybody because the problem didn't need you.

directionInline: Astrid is not visible. The electrical fault is one brief minor spark; by Panel 5 the smoke has stopped. The wall strike cracks the plastic casing once, with the household reaction carrying the impact.

summary: Carrie offers Bjorn a voluntary temporal-arrival support group, and he agrees only after she makes clear that no form, housing rule or compliance requirement is attached.
settingText: Safe Cave table, then the apartment-building stoop later the same day.

panelPlan.action: The cracked power strip sits inside a trash bag off to one side. Carrie and Bjorn sit across from each other with no folder between them.
After Bjorn’s immediate refusal, Carrie keeps her hands off the bare table and watches him; no paperwork sits between them.
Carrie puts both hands flat on the bare table while listing “No form. No compliance box. No housing condition.”
Bjorn’s shoulders drop a fraction; his eyes move to the bagged broken power strip and then back to Carrie.
Later, Carrie holds the building door. Bjorn comes out already dressed in his coat and passes her toward the stairs while delivering his complaint about the meeting.

dialogueInline.text: DTI runs a group for temporal arrivals.
No.
I haven't told you what it is.
You used the voice you use before forms.
No form. No compliance box. No housing condition. People who had a life, and then didn't.
What do they do there?
Mostly argue about what that means.
If it is poorly led, I will leave.
That's actually one of the rules.

summary: At his first group meeting, Bjorn assumes a person from 1987 lost less than he did and is forced to confront how completely one instant can erase a life.
settingText: Plain community-center multipurpose room: mismatched stackable chairs, folding table, coffee urn, bulletin board, radiator and mixed fluorescent/daylight. No therapy-office staging.

panelPlan.action: Eight mismatched chairs make an imperfect circle. Ordinary displaced adults sit casually. Bjorn sits too upright. Group Facilitator occupies an ordinary chair, not a head position. Coffee urn and paper cups sit behind them.
1987 Participant speaks while holding one subtle late-1980s personal object; their current clothes are practical contemporary layers.
Bjorn turns toward the participant, tilts his head and narrows his eyes before answering immediately.
The participant's mouth tightens; they square their shoulders and hold Bjorn's gaze.
The participant keeps steady eye contact. Bjorn’s eyes widen slightly and his jaw relaxes; after a beat he answers the literal wording.

dialogueInline.text: I came through from 1987.
Then your loss is small. You knew this world almost as it is.
My little brother was eight. He's sixty-two. My parents are dead. I'm thirty-four.
Don't call me ancient just because your number is bigger.
I did not call you ancient.
You did it with your face.

directionInline: Group Facilitator remains seated in the same chair circle as everyone else. Background participants wear ordinary contemporary practical clothing with no historical-costume styling.
